Requirement [14.6.3](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v146-http2)

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **14.6.3** | [ADDED] Verify that a full CRLF (\r\n) sequence is property neutralized inside a HTTP/2 header.  | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 113 |


I expect it to be typo, but to be sure.. `property` vs `properly`

Added requirement, commit by @svdb-ncc via https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/commit/367d6feb812d072c2837293066230c8b8f894b4b

I think the word `properly` does not give any extra meaning to requirement. Is the meaning for `neutralized` different from `properly neutralized`?

## Proposal at the moment:

(Additionally removed extra space after requirement text).

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **14.6.3** | [ADDED] Verify that a full CRLF (\r\n) sequence is neutralized inside a HTTP/2 header. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 113 |


## "Neutralized"

What is the precise meaning for the word neutralized here? sanitized? encoded?

comments.body:
I do not want to be prescriptive towards a particular approach as that might differ per context. As in if the CRLF is superfluous, sanitise it. If the CRLF enhances the readability, encode it.
Both are acceptable as long as the CRLF will not de interpreted as a header delimiter.
Thanks for catching the typo though. I agree in dropping the properly as it does not add meaning to the requirement.

title: 14.6.3 - clarify "property neutralized"
